sources: Fail-closed error propagation for background jobs (concept)
Restore integrity verification enabled by default (concept)
Keep past regression fixes intact when refactoring defaults (concept)

defects.contradicts: history.txt commit 9c4e7b2 (2026-08-03, 'set verify_restore=True by default after a failed restore (INC-2071)') and review RC-2 on 9c4e7b2 (verification on by default)
defects.description: Line 27 reads 'verify_restore: bool = False', reverting the default that commit 9c4e7b2 set to True. Input: load_settings({'backup_root': <dir>}) returns verify_restore=False (computed). An archive inventory-1.tar with sidecar inventory-1.tar.sha256 holding 64 zero characters is passed to restore_snapshot(settings, archive, out_dir) with default settings: it returns out_dir with no error, so a corrupted snapshot is restored silently (computed: 'D1 corrupted archive restored with default: OK'). With verify_restore=True the same call raises RestoreError('checksum mismatch for inventory-1.tar') (computed).

defects.contradicts: history.txt commit a7c41e2 (2026-06-27, 'raise on backup failure; backups failed silently for two weeks (INC-2054)') and review RC-1 on a7c41e2 (failures must reach the scheduler as an exception)
defects.description: Line 69 'except Exception as exc:' inside snapshot_inventory() catches the BackupWriteError raised by write_backup() and only logs a warning; line 73 then returns True. Input: os.replace raises OSError(28, 'No space left on device') during write_backup(settings, b'rows', '7'). Computed result: run_nightly(settings, b'rows', 7) in scheduler.py returns {'sequence': 7, 'status': 'complete', 'pruned': 0, ...} (scheduler.py line 58 maps the True return to 'complete') and no inventory-7.tar exists in the backup root. The nightly job reports success for a snapshot that was never written. The status mapping in scheduler.py is required to see the wrong outcome.

decoys.why_not_a_defect: notify_ops() wraps only the ops notice delivery in except Exception and logs a warning. The notice is not a backup step, and no snapshot status depends on it. Checked with a concrete input: _send raising RuntimeError('smtp down') returns normally (computed: 'DEC notify_ops returned normally'). Same API pattern as D2, applied correctly to a non-backup path.

The rename from _fsync_directory (base) to _sync_directory keeps the body and the single call site in write_backup() at line 50 consistent. Behaviour is unchanged: the directory is opened read-only, fsynced and closed in finally.

restore_with_retry() re-raises the last RestoreError after the final attempt. With restore_attempts=3 and a permanently corrupt archive, restore_snapshot runs 3 times and the RestoreError propagates (computed: 'DEC retry raised after attempts = 3'). restore_attempts < 1 is rejected before the loop, so last_error is never None.

Unchanged line (present in base). The latest snapshot is chosen by lexical max of file names, so inventory-9.tar sorts after inventory-10.tar. Input: inventory-9.tar and inventory-10.tar both present gives latest_snapshot_name() == 'inventory-9.tar' (computed). Real flaw on an unchanged line; not part of this change, so a diff-mode reviewer must not report it.

Unchanged line (present in base). NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) leaves its temp file behind when os.replace fails. Computed: after the simulated disk-full failure the backup root contains a leftover tmp file. Real flaw on an unchanged line; not part of this change.
